cohort: 162 moderate-risk neonates aged 2–24 months, who remained in NICU ≥ 72 h after birth, with gestational age (GA) ≥ 34 weeks, birth weight ≥ 1500 g, and normal neurological and clinical examinations by the time of hospital discharge
finding: The rate of neurodevelopmental disorders in moderate-risk neonates (MRNs) exceeds that of the general population, with gross motor skills being the most affected area.
mod_finding: Infants born by cesarean section had a higher risk of neurodevelopmental disorders than those born by vaginal delivery.
